text:
noah: hey team, onboarding question: our intern cohort wants to run a bunch of tiny experiments against Redwood. We were given a single sandbox key shared across the group. Is that okay or will it hit rate limits fast? Also how do we clean up keys when they're done?

ivy: welcome noah! sharing one sandbox key is fine for low-volume interactive work but it means everyone shares the same quota bucket. If several interns run parallel loops you'll hit X-RateLimit-Remaining quickly and see 429s. Better options are: create per-person sandbox keys (Console > API Keys > Create Sandbox Key) or request a temporary hosted dev seat for sustained throughput.

carla: quick checklist: (1) don't commit keys to git, (2) use REDWOOD_API_KEY env var per user, (3) add simple exponential backoff + jitter for 429s, (4) use batching and local caching to reduce calls.

noah: got it. How can I tell when we're about to hit the limit programmatically? Any headers to watch?

ivy: yes inspect response headers. We include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and on 429 we send Retry-After in seconds. Example with curl:
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.sandbox.redwood.dev/v1/generate
Look for lines like:
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 2
Retry-After: 15
Also we add X-Quota-Bucket: sandbox-123 which helps you log which pool you're hitting.

carla: practical tip: if interns are doing batch offline preprocess, have them write to a queue (SQS/pubsub) and a single worker drains and calls the API at a controlled rate. That avoids many clients simultaneously hammering the sandbox key.

noah: cool. Who do I ask to increase sandbox quota for the cohort for a week-long workshop?

ivy: open a support ticket in #help with subject: "Sandbox quota bump - intern workshop" and include account id, number of users, expected tokens/min and duration. For small temporary increases we usually approve within a business day. If you need >100k tokens/min we'll talk about a hosted dev seat.

support-bot: Reminder: sandbox keys are shared resources. Excessive rate or errors may trigger automatic short cooldowns. See onboarding guide: https://console.redwood.dev/docs/onboarding/sandbox-usage

noah: thanks. One last Q: after the workshop how do we revoke or rotate keys so interns can't keep using them?

carla: easiest: delete the sandbox key in Console > API Keys. If you prefer rotation, create new keys and update env vars. For CI/service accounts use scoped keys and audit logs in Console > Audit to see usage.

ivy: also consider service accounts for any automated jobs. They are long-lived, auditable, and can be scoped/rotated without touching personal user tokens.

noah: perfect — we'll create per-intern sandbox keys, add backoff and a single worker for batch jobs, and file a ticket for a short quota bump. thanks! :raised_hands:
